output.needs: The claim's detail that registries are cross-checked for linked entities supplies the mechanism; the disqualification consequence itself is not stated in the claim.

claims_a: Magnesium glycinate 500mg nightly starting Sept 5 improved sleep within 2-3 days: decreased middle-night waking, longer continuous rest.
Oura ring captures HRV, resting heart rate, deep sleep %, REM %, sleep latency, and movement metrics.
First week with Oura ring: 7.2 average hours sleep, 75% deep sleep, 65 bpm resting heart rate.
Cannot yet separate improvement source among supplement, ring measurement, or their combination; both started simultaneously.
Daily morning logging of bedtime, wake time, quality 1-10, and notes paired with daily ring sync.
Plan to continue both supplement and ring tracking for 2-3 weeks to assess stability and persistence of improvements.

output.connection: Continuing both supplement and ring tracking together for 2-3 weeks will not resolve the stated confound; only a deliberate stop of one variable (e.g., a brief magnesium pause) can isolate its effect.
output.mechanism: The confound exists because both started on the same day; holding both constant going forward preserves the confound rather than breaking it, since only varying one input while holding the other fixed can attribute the effect.
output.testable_implication: Schedule a 3-5 day magnesium washout during week 2 or 3, keep Oura logging running, and compare waking frequency and continuous-rest metrics to the on-supplement days.
output.needs: the explicit statement that supplement and ring tracking began simultaneously and cannot yet be separated, plus the plan to continue both unchanged.

claims_a: Interface novelty, not data personalization, drove engagement lift in client eval.

Studies require measurement infrastructure without intervention to avoid measuring the measurement itself.

output.mechanism: The control-arm result already isolates personalization's marginal effect at zero; scaling a component whose ablation showed no engagement drop mechanically implies added cost without a corresponding lift, unless a different metric (e.g. retention, monetization) is the real target.
output.testable_implication: Ask the client which metric justifies scaling personalization if not engagement, and check whether that metric was measured in the same control-arm study before approving the build-out.
output.needs: The claim supplies both the causal isolation (control arm null result) and the client's stated intent to scale despite it, which together expose the decision as unsupported by the study's own data.

claims_a: Simultaneous reconnection of multiple sensors after power loss causes gateway packet drops.
Random 50-500ms transmission delays per sensor eliminate packet loss during power recovery.
Gateway performs well during normal operation but drops packets under simultaneous sensor reconnection.
System remained stable for three days with no packet loss after deploying delay fix.
Workshop test with 12 sensors showed 80% packet loss during post-outage reconnection.

output.connection: The 50-500ms jitter window was validated only at 12 simultaneous sensors; a larger fleet raises collision probability within that same fixed window, so the fix's headroom is unproven beyond N=12.
output.mechanism: Jitter reduces collisions by spreading reconnections across a fixed time window, but as sensor count grows, the chance that two or more sensors still land within any given sub-slice of that fixed window rises, so a window sized for 12 sensors may not scale linearly to a larger fleet.
output.testable_implication: Rerun the workshop reconnection test with a larger sensor count (e.g., 24 or 36) using the same 50-500ms delay range and check packet loss.
output.needs: the claim supplies the tested count (12), the fixed delay range, and the causal link between simultaneity and drops

claims_a: Four DHT22 sensors and two soil moisture probes across workbench and storage areas push readings every 15 minutes to a Raspberry Pi running Node.js.
Daily summaries (min, max, mean) are automatically aggregated at 2300 UTC each day; raw data persists 30 days on SD card, aggregates on NAS SQLite backup.

22 August schema change added collection window ID tags to catch sensor sync drift after reconnection events.

output.connection: The 22 Aug window-ID tags catch sensor sync drift after reconnects, not probe calibration drift like the north shelf's, so that drift needs a separate detection method, not schema tagging.
output.mechanism: Sync drift is a timing misalignment from reconnection events, caught by tagging collection windows. Calibration drift is a sensor's readings deviating from true values over time, unrelated to timestamps, so the same tags cannot flag it.
output.testable_implication: Check whether the north shelf probe's readings have any 22 Aug window-ID flags; if none, set up a separate rule (e.g. threshold vs. known baseline) to auto-detect calibration drift.
output.needs: The claim supplies both the stated purpose of the 22 Aug schema change and the separate, unresolved north probe drift issue as two distinct facts.

claims_a: Fraudsters execute three or more card transactions in ten minutes; legitimate users typically max two.

Multiple high-value charges clustered in time indicate fraud even when daily total stays within limits.
Flagged transactions undergo manual review checking merchant coherence, location data, and card repeat patterns.
Current fraud detection flags about 70% of known compromises before settlement completion.

output.connection: The 30% of compromises caught only after settlement likely paced transactions at or below the 2-per-10-minute threshold, structurally evading the velocity rule.
output.mechanism: Velocity flagging fires only at 3+ transactions in 10 minutes; any fraud sequence held to 2 or fewer per window can never trigger it, so the residual post-settlement catches are exactly the threshold-evading cases.
output.testable_implication: This week, pull timing data for the 30% of compromises caught only after settlement and check whether their per-10-minute transaction counts stayed at or below 2.
output.needs: The exact 3-in-10-minute threshold plus the 70% pre-settlement catch rate, combined.

claims_a: Protocol specifies weekly maximum dose with no daily distribution guidance.
Tracking is done via spreadsheet recording date, dose amount, and cumulative weekly total.
Weekly tracking resets every Monday in 4-week cycles; current window is Sept 1-13.
User skips doses then takes double dose the next day, staying within weekly totals.
Tracker displays only weekly sum and hides daily clustering or consistency patterns.
Weekly reset structure eliminates month-to-month historical view of dosing patterns.

output.connection: Staying within the weekly max does not guarantee safety: doubling a skipped dose the next day roughly doubles single-dose exposure, even though the weekly total looks compliant.
output.mechanism: A weekly cap is likely calibrated assuming roughly even daily intake; concentrating two doses into one day raises peak exposure independent of the weekly sum, a risk the total-only limit does not address.
output.testable_implication: Check the drug label or ask the prescriber whether a maximum single dose or minimum interval between doses exists, then flag any days in the Sept 1-13 window where a doubled dose was taken.
output.needs: That the protocol regulates only the weekly total with no daily guidance, and that the actual practice clusters doses (skip then double) rather than spreading them evenly.

output.testable_implication: Split this week's outreach test into two variants sent to skip-event customers: a pure re-engagement reminder versus a frictionless one-click restart link, then compare response rates.
output.needs: The unresolved disengagement-vs-friction question and the specific design of the planned skip-event outreach test.

output.testable_implication: This week, check whether a single missed log on any day (not just near day 19) automatically triggers an extra reminder before a second consecutive day gets missed.

claims_a: 8 TMP36 sensors with 1 DHT22 reference calibrated monthly against certified handheld unit
Monthly recalibration against DHT22 reference catches typical 0.3°C yearly drift before it compounds

output.needs: the claim's pairing of battery swaps and relocation tests in one cycle, plus the single-read ±0.5°C alarm threshold.

output.needs: The absence of one authoritative source for the gates, combined with the fact that gate failures are currently discovered only after submission.
